 Bengaluru: EPIC numbers of voters deleted during SIR reassigned to others
 Vartha Bharati 20 Nov 2026 5:59 PM IST share Bengaluru: Cases in which the Elector Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers of individuals deleted from the electoral roll have been allotted to others have come to light in Bengaluru. An investigative report by The Hindu has uncovered at least 290 cases where the EPIC numbers of people dropped from the list during the 'Special Intensive Revision' (SIR) appear against the names of other individuals in the final electoral roll.
 An EPIC number that was used to identify one person prior to the SIR process is now being used to identify another. In other words, even after a name was deleted from the electoral roll, the card number was retained and assigned to someone else.
 The names of certain individuals were removed from the electoral roll during the SIR after marking them as 'Absent, Shifted, Dead, or Duplicate' (ASDD). However, their EPIC numbers have shown up against other people's names in the final list.
 The Election Commission of India’s (ECI) Electoral Registration Officers’ Manual explicitly prohibits the reuse of an EPIC number once assigned to a person. The manual states that the software used to generate EPIC numbers must maintain a record of already-issued numbers and ensure that a number once used is not used again.
 An EPIC number allotted to one individual must not be given to another. The Election Commission has also stated that all efforts must be made to ensure universality, uniqueness, and permanence in voter identification numbers.
 These cases were detected by comparing the ASDD list with the final SIR electoral roll. Such discrepancies came to light when checking whether the EPIC numbers of individuals removed from the list were recorded against other names in the final roll. Several such cases were found in Bengaluru’s Dasarahalli Assembly constituency.
 Shashikumar, who was a voter in Part No. 103 of Dasarahalli, had been removed from the list after being marked as 'Dead'. However, his EPIC number has now been allotted to Chandramma, who is registered in Part No. 273 of the same constituency.
 Similarly, Roopa, a voter in Part No. 107, was dropped from the list after being marked as 'Absent'. Her EPIC number is now recorded against the name of Pallavi, who is registered in Part No. 174.
 The Hindu has submitted a sample of EPIC numbers to the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) seeking clarification on these discrepancies. CEO V. Anbu Kumar, stating that they will look into these cases, said that no comment can be made on the matter before the verification is completed.
